question: What is the maximum period of imprisonment that can be given in a summary trial under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, irrespective of the punishment specified for the offence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3 months**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, governs summary trials, which are trials conducted for minor offences to ensure speedy justice. 
 
• Under the BNSS, 2023, the **maximum period of imprisonment** that can be awarded in a summary trial is limited to **3 months**, irrespective of the punishment prescribed for the specific offence under general law. 
 
• Summary trials are conducted for offences that are less serious in nature, ensuring that the judicial process is expedited without compromising fairness and legality. 
 
• As per the BNSS, the purpose of restricting the imprisonment to 3 months is to **avoid excessive punishment** for minor offences and to streamline the judicial process for such cases. 
 
• This provision helps in reducing the burden on courts and ensures that resources are efficiently utilized for more severe cases. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Summary Trial:** 
 
• A summary trial refers to a judicial process where cases are disposed of quickly, focusing on minor offences with simplified procedures. 
 
• It is generally used for offences that do not require detailed investigation or extended court proceedings. 
 
• Examples of offences tried under summary trials include minor theft, public nuisance, and traffic violations. 
 
 

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023:** 
 
• The BNSS, 2023, is a revised and comprehensive code introduced to replace the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) in India. 
 
• It aims to modernize and streamline the judicial system while ensuring the protection of citizens' rights. 
 
• The code incorporates provisions to ensure faster disposal of cases, improved victim rights, and effective law enforcement mechanisms. 
 
 

 
• **Offences Eligible for Summary Trial:** 
 
• Offences punishable by imprisonment of less than 2 years are typically eligible for summary trials. 
 
• Examples include petty theft, public disturbances, and non-serious traffic violations. 
 
• The discretion to try an offence summarily lies with the magistrate, depending on the nature and circumstances of the case. 
 
 

 
• **Benefits of Summary Trials:** 
 
• They reduce the judicial backlog by disposing of minor cases quickly. 
 
• They ensure that individuals accused of minor offences do not face prolonged legal battles or undue harassment. 
 
• They allow courts to focus their resources on more serious and complex cases. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Comparison with CrPC:** 
 
• Under the earlier Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), summary trials also had a maximum imprisonment limit of 3 months for minor offences. 
 
• The BNSS, 2023, continues this provision to maintain consistency in handling minor cases. 
 
 

 
• **Judicial Oversight:** 
 
• Even in summary trials, the judiciary ensures that procedural fairness and justice are maintained. 
 
• Accused persons have the right to present their case, call witnesses, and cross-examine prosecution witnesses. 
 
 

 
• **Exception to Maximum Limit:** 
 
• For certain offences, if the law prescribes lesser punishment than 3 months, the magistrate cannot exceed that limit during sentencing. 
 
• This ensures adherence to the principles of proportionality in punishment.
